mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust residential construction activity, signaling strong consumer confidence and demand for durable goods, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate revenue growth accelerates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST increases by at least 1.0% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 2.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that compresses equity valuations through higher discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate borrowing costs rise.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through joint demand effects.
failure_condition: The joint effect of UNRATE decline and PAYEMS increase fails to produce positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or interaction term p-value > 0.05 in regression.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals manufacturing slowdown and reduced corporate capacity utilization, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as profit growth expectations decline.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines during late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month rise in CPIAUCSL above 0.2% indicates persistent inflation, prompting central bank rate hikes that depress equity valuations through higher real rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises by at least 0.2% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) fall by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate revenue growth decelerates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS falls by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates broad-based demand strength, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through combined effects on consumer spending and business investment.
failure_condition: The joint effect of HOUST and RSAFS increases fails to produce positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or interaction term p-value > 0.05 in regression.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 6.5%), a decline in unemployment rate signals improving labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 6.5 and UNRATE declines.
